name: azure-templates-navigator
description: Hover, validate, autocomplete and navigate Azure Pipelines YAML templates — including templates from other repositories, which are downloaded automatically.

azure-templates-navigator.requiredParame.description: Hex color used to highlight required parameters in hover tooltips.

azure-templates-navigator.diagnostics.en.description: Validate template call sites (missing required / unknown parameters, type mismatches, disallowed values, missing templates).

azure-templates-navigator.diagnostics.un.description: Warn about parameters a template declares but never references.

azure-templates-navigator.changes.enable.description: Compare the workspace with the commit your work started from (where this branch split from the branch it was created from, or a base you choose). The Pipelines view's *My changes* mode and the verdict above each pipeline then show the problems your changes added and fixed. Needs a git repository.

azure-templates-navigator.changes.dimExi.description: Show the errors and warnings that were already there before your changes (at the commit your work started from) as information, so the Problems panel's errors and warnings are the ones your changes added. The Pipelines view and the verdicts keep the real severities.

azure-templates-navigator.azure.enabled.markdownDescription: Offer to check the pipelines your changes reach with Azure DevOps itself (*Check in Azure DevOps* in the Pipelines view's *My changes* mode). Azure compiles each pipeline at the base and with your changes, without running it. Your changed YAML files are pushed to a `refs/atn/preview/…` ref first (no branch, no CI run); you confirm each check. Signs in with the Azure CLI (`az login --allow-no-subscriptions`).

azure-templates-navigator.azure.keepSnap.markdownDescription: Keep the `refs/atn/preview/…` refs that hold your changes after a check in Azure DevOps (by default they are deleted when the check is done).

azure-templates-navigator.azure.azPath.markdownDescription: Path to the Azure CLI (`az`), used to sign in to Azure DevOps. Empty: `az` on the PATH.

azure-templates-navigator.completion.req.description: When completing a template path, also insert a `parameters:` block with the template's required parameters (skipped when the call already has one).

azure-templates-navigator.graph.rootPath.description: Sub-folder (relative to the workspace root) shown in the workspace-wide Template Graph. Empty = whole workspace.

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.a.markdownDescription: Automatically download repositories referenced via `resources.repositories` (e.g. `template: x.yml@templates`) when they are not available locally. Uses your normal `git` credentials.

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.c.markdownDescription: Folder where downloaded repositories are kept. Empty = `~/.azure-templates-navigator/repos` (shared by VS Code, IntelliJ and the `atn` CLI).

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.r.description: Re-fetch downloaded repositories in the background when older than this many hours. 0 = never.

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.p.markdownDescription: Use a clone that sits next to your repository (`../<repo-name>`) instead of the download cache when one exists, so edits in your working copy are picked up immediately.

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.u.markdownDescription: Clone URL overrides, keyed by alias, repository `name:` or repository name. Example: `{ "myorg/templates": "git@github.com:myorg/templates.git" }`. Can also be committed in `.azure-templates-navigator.json`.

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.l.markdownDescription: Map a repository (alias, `name:` or repository name) to a local folder. Example: `{ "templates": "~/src/pipeline-templates" }`.

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.a.markdownDescription: Azure DevOps organization hosting `type: git` repositories. Only needed when it can't be inferred from your repository's `origin` remote (e.g. your code lives on GitHub).
Default Azure DevOps project for `type: git` repositories declared without a project (`name: repo`).

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.g.markdownDescription: Host name for `type: githubenterprise` repositories, e.g. `github.mycompany.com`.

azure-templates-navigator.repositories.g.description: Path to the git executable used to download repositories.

azure-templates-navigator.server.path.description: Advanced: path to a custom 'atn' language server binary (for development).

commands.title: Show How the Expanded Pipeline Changed

viewsWelcome.contents:
No `resources.repositories` found in this workspace.
Templates referenced as `path.yml@alias` are downloaded here automatically.

No pipelines found in this workspace.
A pipeline is a YAML file with pipeline-level keys such as `trigger`, `pr`, `schedules`, `resources`, `extends` or `pool` that no other file uses as a template.

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with Azure Templates Navigator
walkthroughs.description: What the extension does for your Azure Pipelines YAML, one feature at a time.

steps.title: Will this pipeline run?
steps.description:
Every pipeline shows a verdict above its first line, covering the pipeline and every template it reaches. Click it to list the problems. The **Pipelines** view lists every pipeline in the workspace, failing first.
[Open the Pipelines View](command:azure-templates-navigator.pipelinesView.focus)

steps.title: What did my changes break?
steps.description:
When many pipelines already fail, click **Show My Changes** in the title of the **Pipelines** view. It compares your work with where it started (where your branch split from the branch it came from, committed or not): the files you changed, the problems they added and fixed, and the pipelines they reach, with the total underneath. The **Diagnostics** view follows the same switch. Click the *Since* row to compare with another branch or with your last commit. Turn on "changes.dimExistingProblems" to show the older problems as information in the Problems panel.
[Show My Changes](command:azure-templates-navigator.showMyChanges)

steps.title: See a template's parameters
steps.description:
Hover a "template:" line to see the template's parameters, with their types, defaults and allowed values. Required ones are highlighted. Ctrl/Cmd+click opens the template.
[Search Templates](command:azure-templates-navigator.searchTemplates)

steps.title: Complete a template call in one go
steps.description:
Completing a template path also inserts a "parameters:" block with the template's required parameters. Press Tab to move between the values.
[Completion Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22azure-templates-navigator.completion%22%5D)

media.altText: Complete a template call in one go

steps.title: Fix template calls from the problem
steps.description:
Missing required parameters, misspelled names ("did you mean"), values outside "values:" and missing templates are reported as you type. Most of them have a quick fix: press Ctrl+. (Cmd+. on macOS) on the problem.
[Open the Problems View](command:workbench.actions.view.problems)

media.altText: Fix template calls from the problem

steps.title: Who uses this template?
steps.description: Before you change a template, check who calls it. The "N usages" lens above the template lists its call sites, and Find All References (Shift+Alt+F12) works on templates and on their parameters.

steps.title: Follow the chain from pipeline to template
steps.description: On a template, *Show Call Hierarchy* (Shift+Alt+H) lists the templates that call it, the pipelines that call those, and so on up to every pipeline that reaches it. Its toggle shows the other direction: everything a pipeline calls.

media.altText: Follow the chain from pipeline to template

steps.title: See how pipelines and templates connect
steps.description:
The **Template Graph** draws the current file with its callers and callees, or the whole workspace. Bigger nodes are used more. Click a node to light up everything that reaches it and everything it calls, and filter to problems, kinds or repositories.
[Open the Graph](command:azure-templates-navigator.expandTemplateGraph)

media.altText: See how pipelines and templates connect

steps.title: Templates from other repositories
steps.description:
"template: x.yml@templates" works like a local template: the repository is downloaded into a shared cache with your normal git credentials, and refreshed in the background. The **Repositories** view shows each one's state and the templates you use from it.
[Open the Repositories View](command:azure-templates-navigator.repositoriesView.focus)

steps.title: When a repository can't be found
steps.description: Most repositories need no setup. If one shows as failed or unconfigured in the **Repositories** view, or your templates live in a folder rather than their own repository, commit ".azure-templates-navigator.json" at the repository root. "urls" pins an alias's clone URL. "localPaths" points an alias at a folder, which is then read as is, with no download. Everyone gets the same mapping, in VS Code, IntelliJ and the "atn" CLI.

steps.title: Stats for template owners
steps.description:
The **Stats** view shows problems by type, the most used and most mis-called templates, templates nothing references, and counts per repository. Click a row to open the file, or *Show in Graph* to see it in context.
[Open the Stats View](command:azure-templates-navigator.statsView.focus)

steps.title: The same checks in CI
steps.description: The "atn" binary behind this extension also runs in a terminal or a pipeline: "atn check" prints every pipeline's verdict and exits with 1 on errors. "--format azure" turns the problems into annotations on the run. See the [CLI documentation](https://github.com/qSharpy/azure-templates-navigator#cli).
